analysis.investment_thesis: IIFL Capital Services is a fast grower riding India's secular capital markets expansion, trading at a PEG of just 0.79 (P/E 17 / 21.6% earnings CAGR) — exactly the kind of mispriced growth I look for. The combination of 31.6% ROE, expanding operating margins, and a simple story (India's retail investor boom) makes this a compelling GARP candidate.
key_strengths: PEG of 0.79 — earnings growing 21.6% CAGR while P/E sits at 17, classic underpriced growth
Exceptional profitability: ROE 31.6%, ROCE 33.3%, operating margin 38% — this is a high-quality capital-light franchise
India tailwind is visible from the street: demat accounts, IPO pipeline, and HNI wealth management are all booming structural stories
key_risks: Cyclicality is the killer — broking/IB revenues collapse when markets turn; FY2023 OCF was -793 Cr, showing how fast the story can reverse
Promoter stake at only 30.93% is low for an Indian financial services firm — limited skin in the game is a yellow flag
Debt/Equity at 0.62 is right at my limit, and borrowings nearly tripled (486→1,742 Cr) in two years — leverage is rising fast
red_flags: OCF negative in 2 of last 5 years (FY23: -793 Cr, FY24: -118 Cr) — inconsistent cash conversion in a high-margin business is puzzling
Revenue growth decelerated to ~13.7% in FY25 (2,217→2,520 Cr) even as profit growth accelerated — mix shift or sustainability question
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Peter Lynch's first question is always "What's the story?" — here it's crystal clear: India's capital markets are democratizing at speed, and IIFL Capital sits at the intersection of retail broking, HNI wealth distribution, and investment banking. The PEG of 0.79 is the headline number — a business compounding earnings at 21.6% seven-year CAGR available at just 17x earnings. Net profit nearly tripled from 250 Cr (FY23) to 713 Cr (FY25), and operating margins expanded from sub-35% to 38%+. This is a fast grower that the market hasn't fully repriced yet.

The concern Lynch would have: this is a semi-cyclical fast grower, not a pure compounder. The FY23 cash flow disaster (-793 Cr OCF) shows exactly how quickly the story breaks when market volumes dry up. Rising borrowings (486 Cr → 1,742 Cr in three years) add financial leverage on top of operating leverage — in a down market, that's a double-edged sword. I'd want to own this in a diversified portfolio and size it accordingly, not bet the farm. The low promoter holding (31%) means management doesn't suffer proportionately when things go wrong.
